transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Li (Redwood SE), Mark Tanner (CISO, NovaHealth), Lena Ortiz (Security Manager, NovaHealth), Devon Park (Cloud Engineer, NovaHealth)

Summary:
High-level SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture review focused on evidence sharing, trust center access, controls mapping for NovaHealth's upcoming vendor assessment. Customer asked specific questions about SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit log retention, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, and data residency (EU/US). Redwood team committed to providing reports, trust center read-only link, and controls mapping spreadsheet; scheduled a follow-up workshop to map controls to NovaHealth's evidence requirements.

Topics:
- SOC 2 Type II report availability and scope
- ISO 27001 certificate and statement of applicability
- Trust Center: how to provision, what is available
- Controls mapping (CCM/ISO mapping to NovaHealth control IDs)
- RBAC and SSO (SAML/Okta integration)
- Audit logs: retention, access, export capabilities
- Encryption: KMS, key management, BYOK options
- Data residency & VPC/private deployment options
- Evidence sharing workflow and NDA/contractual questions

Transcript body:
00:00 - Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intro, I'm Jordan on the AE side, Priya and Marco from our security and infra team.
00:06 - Mark Tanner: Hi, Mark here, CISO at NovaHealth. We've got Lena and Devon with me. We're doing vendor due diligence, SOC2 and ISO primarily.
00:12 - Priya Nair: Great. The goal for today is a posture review — walk through what artifacts we can share, get aligned on scope, and identify any gaps for your audit.
00:20 - Lena Ortiz: To be clear, our security team needs SOC 2 Type II covering data handling in production, plus ISO 27001 cert if available. Also need a controls mapping to our internal control IDs.
00:28 - Jordan Ellis: Totally. We have a SOC 2 Type II for the Redwood hosted API and a current ISO 27001 certificate. We'll share the redacted report and cert. Priya will handle the trust center access.
00:38 - Devon Park: On data residency — we must keep PHI-related metadata in EU regions. Do you support region pinning or private deployments?
00:45 - Marco Li: Yes, we support region pinning for hosted endpoints and also Private (VPC) deployments for stricter isolation. For EU residency we can route requests to the EU region or offer private deployments if you need physical isolation.
00:55 - Mark Tanner: Good. On encryption, can you confirm KMS and BYOK? Our policy requires customer-managed keys for some workloads.
01:02 - Priya Nair: We support integration with customer KMS providers — e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS — and offer BYOK for Private deployments. For hosted API there are options for envelope encryption; we'll attach the design doc.
01:14 - Lena Ortiz: Audit logs — we need 1 year of immutable logs for API calls and admin actions. How long do you retain logs and can we export them?
01:21 - Marco Li: Default retention is 90 days in the hosted product but we offer extended retention add-ons and log export APIs. For Dedicated/Private, retention and export policies are configurable and can meet 12 months. We'll note this in the controls mapping.
01:35 - Mark Tanner: SSO — we use Okta SAML, want RBAC scoping so only certain teams can call models with PHI. How granular is RBAC?
01:43 - Priya Nair: RBAC supports per-route and per-key roles, and you can bind SAML groups to roles. For Private/Dedicated you can also integrate with your IdP via SCIM for group sync. We'll share a sample RBAC policy and the SAML setup doc.
01:55 - Jordan Ellis: There was a question about auditability of model changes and version pinning — if you need to know exact model binary and quantization used for inference for compliance.
02:03 - Devon Park: Yes, we need reproducibility — which model version, container image, quantization, and runtime.
02:09 - Marco Li: Our serving runtime logs model version, rollout ID, and container hash in audit logs. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide signed attestations for rollouts.
02:20 - Mark Tanner: For the SOC controls mapping, do you provide a mapping to CC or ISO control IDs?
02:25 - Priya Nair: We maintain a controls mapping XLS that maps SOC 2 CC sections and ISO 27001 Annex controls to Redwood artifacts/evidence (policies, diagrams, configs). We'll populate it with NovaHealth in the follow-up workshop.
02:36 - Lena Ortiz: On evidence sharing: can we get read-only access to a trust center with redacted reports, and an evidence repository where we can pull logs?
02:43 - Jordan Ellis: We'll provision a trust center read-only link. Evidence repo access is scoped — for hosted customers we provide packaged evidence and exports; for Dedicated/Private we can grant more direct access or ship bundles.
02:55 - Mark Tanner: Any third-party pen test or vulnerability scan reports we can see?
03:00 - Marco Li: We have annual external pentest summaries and internal vuln scan attestations. Full reports are available under NDA; summaries are in the trust center.
03:08 - Devon Park: Regarding network controls — do you support VPC peering or private connectivity?
03:12 - Priya Nair: Yes, for Private we offer VPC peering, private connectivity and even on-prem appliance deployments for very specific regulated use cases. We also support egress control lists and restrict outbound connections.
03:24 - Lena Ortiz: A couple of risk items: how do you handle data retention and data deletion requests? We need proof of deletion for certain data types.
03:31 - Marco Li: We log deletion operations and can provide attestations. For Private deployments you control retention; for hosted we have documented deletion flows and can include a deletion certificate where appropriate.
03:42 - Jordan Ellis: Timeline — what's realistic to get initial artifacts in your procurement packet?
03:45 - Lena Ortiz: We need a vendor package by next Friday (2026-03-13) to present to our procurement board. Ideally SOC2, ISO cert, controls mapping draft, RBAC doc, and KMS/BYOK info.
03:55 - Jordan Ellis: We'll prioritize sending SOC2 and ISO cert within two business days and the trust center link + controls mapping template by Friday. Then schedule the 1-hour workshop next week.
04:05 - Mark Tanner: Perfect. A couple of quick clarifying questions — are there data processing addendums and DPA templates?
04:10 - Priya Nair: Yes, we have a standard DPA and can negotiate required clauses for data residency and subprocessors. We'll attach the DPA and list of subprocessors in the trust center.
04:20 - Devon Park: For logs exports — can we pull them into our SIEM? Is there a push integration?
04:24 - Marco Li: We support S3/Blob export and a webhook/forwarder for streaming logs to a SIEM. For high-volume setups we recommend Dedicated with local export to your log store.
04:34 - Jordan Ellis: Any regulatory red flags from your side? Specific controls we cannot meet?
04:38 - Priya Nair: Nothing major — some items like BYOK for hosted (not full native BYOK) and physical separation requirements (if you need cert-level on-prem isolation) might push you toward Private. We'll call those out.
04:50 - Lena Ortiz: OK, that helps. We'll review the artifacts and bring any follow-ups to the workshop.
04:55 - Jordan Ellis: Great. I'll recap and list action items.
05:00 - Jordan Ellis: Recap: Jordan sends SOC2 & ISO cert, Priya does trust center + controls mapping template, Marco adds details on logs & KMS, NovaHealth confirms scope & residency. Follow-up workshop week of 2026-03-09.
05:12 - Mark Tanner: Thanks, appreciate it.
05:15 - Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript: Transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "BYO K" for BYOK) and speaker overlaps; timestamps are approximate.
